title.value: Normalization Layers Are All That Sharpness-Aware Minimization Needs
title.justification: The title is explicit in identifying the main focus of the paper, which is the relationship between normalization layers and Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM).
title.quote: Normalization Layers Are All That Sharpness-Aware Minimization Needs

extractions.description: This paper investigates the role of normalization layers in Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), showing that perturbing only these layers in the optimization process can outperform perturbing all parameters. It examines the impact of this approach across different architectures and use cases, highlighting its advantages in computational efficiency and generalization performance.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on the technical optimization of neural networks using normalization layers within SAM, a topic not directly related to environmental applications or sustainability. It is primarily concerned with improving machine learning efficiency, which could indirectly benefit eco-responsible topics but is not the main focus here.
primary_category.quote: Although our findings reaffirm the effectiveness of SAM in improving generalization performance, they cast doubt on whether this is solely caused by reduced sharpness.

secondary_categories.justification: The technical improvements in SAM, while possibly beneficial to energy efficiency in general computational contexts, are not directly tied to specific environmental applications as outlined in the categories.
secondary_categories.quote: We find that SAM-ON obtains enhanced generalization performance compared to conventional SAM (denoted as SAM-all) for ResNet architectures with BatchNorm (Section 4.1) and Vision Transformers with LayerNorm (Section 4.2) on CIFAR data and performs competitively on ImageNet.

primary_sub_category.justification: The work described in the paper does not fit into any eco-responsible sub-category. It focuses on the internal mechanics of deep learning optimization rather than applications in environmental fields.
primary_sub_category.quote: We find that SAM-ON obtains enhanced generalization performance compared to conventional SAM (denoted as SAM-all) for ResNet architectures with BatchNorm (Section 4.1) and Vision Transformers with LayerNorm (Section 4.2) on CIFAR data and performs competitively on ImageNet.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper's contributions are technical, focusing on deep learning algorithm performance, without direct relevance to eco-responsible sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The method of sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) has risen to prominence due to its demonstrated effectiveness and the community’s long-standing interest in flat minima.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's primary focus is on improving a machine learning optimization method, specifically Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), which does not align with the environmental categories listed.
new_primary_category.quote: In this work we show that perturbing only the affine normalization parameters (typically comprising 0.1% of the total parameters) in the adversarial step of SAM can outperform perturbing all of the parameters.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper centers around increasing algorithmic efficiency in SAM by targeting normalization layers, hence improving computational performance and reducing resource use in model training.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Inspired by this we focus on the interplay between SAM and normalization layers and show that for various settings perturbing exclusively the normalization layers of a network (often less than 0.1% of the total parameters) outperforms perturbing all parameters.
